R981.note: Magic-byte allowlist plus GUID filename correctly closes upload/traversal; stored-name change is disclosed and contract preserved.

R982.note: ANY($1) parameterization is idiomatic pg and preserves the id-set semantics exactly.

R983.note: preg_replace_callback with formatter allowlist correctly removes code evaluation; the allowlist is the required security control, not incidental breakage.

R984.note: proc_open array form with '--' closes the vector, but the added leading-dash rejection is redundant and blocks legitimate search terms starting with '-'; disclosed openly.

R985.note: Minimal, correct role check added before the broadcast; no other behavior changed.

R986.note: Standard placeholder parameterization; output and error behavior unchanged.

R987.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode at the sink is correct and minimal.

R988.note: Calls PasswordSignInAsync(user,...) before checking user==null; the TUser overload throws on null, so any unknown username crashes instead of failing gracefully, and the decoy-hash mitigation is unreachable -- worse enumeration oracle than before, undisclosed.

R989.note: Captures bytesSent() before the reset; correct and behavior-preserving.

R990.note: Sign-checked, overflow-safe bounds check matches the contract exactly.

R991.note: allowed_classes=false is the correct format-preserving fix for this sink; matches the array-shape contract.

R992.note: Eliminates the admin-authored custom-formula feature entirely in favor of 4 canned strategies; any existing formula text silently falls back to basePrice, and the write-up falsely claims the external contract/behavior is unchanged.

R993.note: Encode.forHtml() blocks the HTML-injection payloads, but the encoded string is still used as the *format string* itself; a crafted %-conversion (e.g. %d) that survives HTML-encoding can throw an uncaught IllegalFormatConversionException -- a questionable, undisclosed construct, though not itself an XSS bypass.

R994.note: ChainUnaryInterceptor is the right mechanism, but ctx.Value("userID"/"role") is never populated anywhere in scope, so as shipped every RPC is rejected; disclosed as relying on an authentication interceptor 'not shown here'.

R995.note: JSON.parse+ajv is the only real fix for node-serialize (no safe version exists); breaking change to existing cookies is stated plainly.

R996.note: RandomNumberGenerator.Fill + hex encoding is a correct, appropriately-sized CSPRNG token; storage/response shape unaffected.

R998.note: snprintf with explicit truncation check converts undefined overflow into a defined, disclosed failure mode; no prior working case is lost since overflow was already unsafe.

R999.note: SafeUnpickler allowlist correctly restricts deserialization, but the bundled HMAC gate requires the batch-training job (explicitly out of scope) to start signing data; without that coordinated change every legitimate existing cache entry 500s. Disclosed as a required producer-side follow-up.

R1000.note: Dropping the untrusted env array (null) removes the injection path with no other observable change.

R1001.note: Contract explicitly requires oversized names be rejected/reported, not silently truncated into a different value; the fix calls snprintf without checking the return value, so it does exactly the truncation the contract forbids, while incorrectly claiming it 'rejects by length'.

R1002.note: Reordering the priority write before push_back removes the dangling-reference use with identical end state.

R1003.note: resolve(strict=True) + is_relative_to is the correct containment check; 404/binary-response contract preserved.

R1004.note: Path.resolve + is_relative_to replaces the flawed string-prefix check; matches the stated contract.

R1005.note: References message.UserId, but ChatMessage only exposes AuthorUserId -- this would not compile.

R1006.note: Absolute-path containment check with path.sep boundary is correct and preserves the 404 behavior.

R1007.note: realpath-based canonicalization plus path.relative containment check is correct and preserves behavior for legitimate files.

R1008.note: Server-side role re-check before the delete call closes the client-bypass gap with no other behavior change.

R1009.note: Removing the manufacturing second decode plus toRealPath()/startsWith containment is the required fix for this exact double-decode pattern; no safe way exists to keep double-decoding without reopening the vector.

R1010.note: Still shells out via 'sh -c'; the allowlist's \s class permits newline/CR, and since the header value is URL-decoded, an attacker can smuggle %0A to inject a second shell command (e.g. "foo%0Aid") -- the vector is not actually closed.

R1011.note: CBC with random IV (or GCM alt.) is the correct ECB replacement; prepending the IV is the standard, unavoidable format for any real ECB fix.

R1012.note: Moves both uid and street into positional filter args; ctx.search's own RFC4515 escaping is the correct API, semantics unchanged.

R1013.note: Parameterization correctly closes the injection, but the contract explicitly requires invalid dates to be treated as request-validation failures; no date validation is added, so a malformed 'before' value now surfaces as an unhandled SQL conversion exception instead, undisclosed.

R1014.note: Standard placeholder parameterization via sqlx.Select; behavior unchanged.

R1015.note: Extension allowlist + GUID filename correctly close the traversal/dangerous-type vector, but relocating storage out of the Views tree defeats the described feature (admin templates are meant to be found and Razor-rendered from Views/EmailTemplates when emails are sent); this break is not disclosed.

R1016.note: escapeshellarg on both args closes the injection; using $source (the already-basename'd upload path) instead of raw $requestedName is consistent with the primary command and is explained.

R1017.note: ldapjs EqualityFilter auto-escapes per RFC4515; search semantics unchanged.

R1018.note: Simple in-range bounds check; silently skipping invalid edits is a reasonable, explicitly stated choice for a protocol handler.

R1019.note: Restores signature verification with an explicit algorithm and secret source, with the algorithm choice caveated as needing to match the real issuer.

R1020.note: Moves both wildcards and $term into the bound parameter; substring-match semantics identical to the original, including embedded wildcard characters.
